questions.question: Why can a Spring Boot starter be added to pom.xml without a <version> tag?
options: Maven always downloads the newest version
spring-boot-starter-parent manages the versions through spring-boot-dependencies
The IDE fills the version in when you build
questions.explanation: The starter parent inherits from spring-boot-dependencies, which fixes matching versions for Spring Boot's libraries.

questions.question: Which scope makes a library available only while compiling and running tests, and keeps it out of the final JAR?
questions.explanation: test scope is used for test code only, so the library is never packaged with the app.

questions.question: The build section has <finalName>foodrush</finalName> and the project version is 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT. What file does ./mvnw package create?
questions.explanation: finalName replaces the default artifactId-version file name inside target.

questions.question: A pom.xml has spring-boot-starter-webmvc without a version and no <parent> section. What happens when you run ./mvnw package?
options: It builds, using the latest Spring Boot
It builds, but the app will not start
Maven stops with an error that the dependency version is missing
Maven asks you to choose a version
questions.explanation: Without the parent nothing supplies the version, so Maven reports that dependencies.dependency.version is missing.

questions.question: A project builds fine, but java -jar target/app.jar prints: no main manifest attribute. What is the most likely cause?
options: spring-boot-maven-plugin is missing from the build section
The main class needs to be public static
questions.explanation: Without spring-boot-maven-plugin, Maven builds a plain JAR with no main class entry and no libraries inside.
